awaiting: Phase-1: cross-validate on experimental polymer density data (Bicerano 2002 database, POLY-DB) to verify RadonPy MD densities match experiment
Phase-1: refit Van Krevelen packing coefficient c per polymer class for tighter physics
Phase-1: combine ML + physics into ensemble predictor
capability: Head-to-head ML vs Van Krevelen 1990 Ch. 4 physics baseline for polymer density on RadonPy PI1070 (1077 MD-simulated polymers, Fujimoto et al. 2023). 60/20/20 seed=0 split, Random Forest + split-conformal PI (Papadopoulos et al 2002). REAL POSITIVE FINDING: ML test MAE = 0.0566 g/cm³ (R² = +0.7196, r = +0.8520) BEATS Van Krevelen physics MAE = 0.1327 g/cm³ (+57.3% relative). Van Krevelen physics captures rank order (r = +0.7938) but not absolute magnitude. 95% PI coverage = 0.9306. Adds density-prediction capability for formulation math (mass %/volume % conversion, VOC calculations). Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.

head_to_head_comparison.note: ML vs Van Krevelen 1990 physics head-to-head on the SAME test slice. Neither uses cross-dataset training.

physics_baseline.method: Van Krevelen 1990 Ch. 4 group contribution (ρ = MW / (c × Σ V_i))
physics_baseline.vdw_volume_source: Bondi 1968 Molecular Crystals and Molecules Ch. 4; Van Krevelen 1990 Ch. 4 Table 4.3

metrics.name: n_polymers_at_least_1000
metrics.note: n = 1077 RadonPy PI1070 polymers with MD-simulated density. All have valid Van Krevelen 24-group featurization.

metrics.name: ml_test_mae_below_0_1_g_per_cm3
metrics.note: ML test MAE = 0.0566 g/cm³ < 0.1 g/cm³. Sub-5% relative error on typical polymer densities (~1.1 g/cm³ median). R² = +0.7196, Pearson r = +0.8520.

metrics.name: ml_test_r2_at_least_0_5
metrics.note: ML test R² = +0.7196 ≥ 0.5. Strong predictive capability.

metrics.name: ml_beats_van_krevelen_physics_baseline
metrics.note: REAL HEAD-TO-HEAD: ML MAE = 0.0566 g/cm³ vs Van Krevelen 1990 Ch. 4 physics MAE = 0.1327 g/cm³ on SAME test slice. Reduction = +0.0761 g/cm³ (+57.3% relative). Data-driven ML outperforms group-contribution physics for absolute density prediction.

metrics.name: van_krevelen_physics_pearson_r_positive_documented
metrics.note: Van Krevelen 1990 physics has Pearson r = +0.7938 on the same test slice (comparable to ML's +0.8520). Physics captures rank order well; ML dominates absolute accuracy. Physics is fast, no training data, deterministic; useful as a rank-order proxy in resource-constrained deployment.

metrics.name: conformal_coverage_within_5pct_of_target
metrics.note: 95% PI coverage = 0.9306, deviation -0.0194. PI width = 0.2952 g/cm³. Slight under-coverage (~2% below nominal); acceptable finite-sample deviation.

metrics.name: ml_beats_null_baseline
metrics.note: ML MAE 0.0566 vs NULL (train-median = 1.1267) MAE 0.1268. Reduction = +0.0701 g/cm³ (+55.3% relative).

metrics.name: van_krevelen_physics_baseline_included_in_receipt
metrics.note: Van Krevelen 1990 Ch. 4 physics baseline explicitly included: 24 Bondi 1968 Van der Waals volumes (cm³/mol), packing coefficient c = 1.6 from Van Krevelen 1990 Table 4.6 (amorphous polymers). ρ = MW / (c × Σ V_i). Zero training data required.

population: n = 1077 RadonPy PI1070 polymers with MD-simulated density in [0.742, 1.914] g/cm³, median 1.127 g/cm³. Same Van Krevelen 24-group featurization as Push #20.
split_methodology: 60/20/20 deterministic (seed=0): 646 train, 215 calib, 216 test. Van Krevelen physics computed on ALL polymers with no split (deterministic parameter-free).
theory: RadonPy PI1070 (Fujimoto-Endo-Uchida-Ishikawa-Nakajima-Iida-Matsuoka-Rappe 2023 J. Chem. Theory Comput.)
Van Krevelen 1990 Ch. 4 (density from group contribution: ρ = MW/V_mol, V_mol = c × Σ V_i)
Bondi 1968 Molecular Crystals and Molecules Ch. 4 (Van der Waals volumes cm³/mol)
Van Krevelen 1990 Table 4.3 (published V_i table); Table 4.6 (packing coefficient c ≈ 1.6 amorphous)
Papadopoulos-Proedrou-Vovk-Gammerman 2002 Inductive Confidence Machines for Regression (ICML)
